title: AI Adoption Rate Across US Companies
description: Percentage of US firms using AI in production, measured by the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) — the most rigorous measure available. Survey-based estimates from consultancies run 5-10x higher due to self-selected samples.

sources.title: AI Adoption in America: Who, What, and Where
sources.publisher: Journal of Economics & Management Strategy (McElheran, Li, Brynjolfsson et al.)
sources.excerpt: Just under 6% of firms nationwide used AI as of 2017. Yet most very large firms (over 5,000 employees) reported at least some AI use. Employment-weighted adoption was just over 18%. Based on the 2018 Annual Business Survey of 850,000 firms linked to the Longitudinal Business Database.

sources.title: The State of AI in 2023: Generative AI's Breakout Year
sources.excerpt: One-third of respondents say their organizations are using gen AI regularly in at least one business function. AI adoption overall at 55% of survey respondents.

sources.title: Business Trends and Outlook Survey: AI Module Q3 2023
sources.excerpt: 3.8% of US firms reported using AI in production. An additional 6.4% were in testing/pilot phase. Adoption highest in information (18%) and professional services (12%).

sources.title: The State of AI in Early 2024
sources.excerpt: 72% of organizations surveyed now use AI in at least one function, up from 55% the prior year. Generative AI adoption doubled.

sources.title: Business Trends and Outlook Survey: AI Module Q2 2024
sources.excerpt: AI usage among US firms rose to 6.6%, with an additional 9.1% in testing. Information sector at 24%, finance/insurance at 15%.

sources.title: State of Generative AI in the Enterprise Q3 2024
sources.excerpt: 79% of enterprise leaders expect gen AI to transform their industry within 3 years. 42% have gen AI in production, up from 22% a year earlier.

sources.title: The State of AI in 2025
sources.excerpt: AI is now a core part of business strategy for 78% of respondents. 65% report measurable revenue or cost impact from AI deployments.

sources.title: Business Trends and Outlook Survey: AI Module Q2 2025
sources.excerpt: US firm AI usage in production reached 10.2%, with 14.8% in testing. Large firms (500+ employees) at 28%. Adoption accelerating across all sectors.

sources.title: Microsoft 2024 Annual Report
sources.excerpt: Over 60,000 Azure AI customers by end of FY2024, growing nearly 60% YoY. Azure AI revenue reached a $13 billion annual run rate, growing 175% YoY.

sources.title: Salesforce Announces Strong Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2024 Results
sources.excerpt: Salesforce Einstein platform serves over 200 billion AI predictions per day across Customer 360 applications. Einstein 1 platform enables AI-powered apps with low-code development and generative AI assistants.

sources.title: The Anthropic Economic Index: Measuring AI's Real-World Impact
sources.excerpt: Census Bureau rigorous measure finds 9.7% of firms actively using AI, while broader surveys report 78%. Adoption gap driven by definitional differences in what counts as AI use.

sources.title: Stanford AI Index Report 2025
sources.excerpt: 78% of organizations report using AI in at least one business function. Enterprise AI spending grew 45% YoY globally.

sources.title: AI at Work Is Here. Now Comes the Hard Part
sources.excerpt: 75% of knowledge workers now use AI tools. Adoption in enterprises with 500+ employees reached 60%, up from 40% a year prior.

sources.title: The Labor Market Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence
sources.publisher: Stanford / World Bank (Hartley, Jolevski, Melo, Moore)
sources.excerpt: 35.9% of US workers used generative AI by December 2025. Adoption concentrated among younger, college-educated, higher-earning employees.

sources.title: The Unequal Adoption of ChatGPT Exacerbates Existing Inequalities Among Workers
sources.excerpt: Half of workers in AI-exposed occupations have used ChatGPT; adoption unequal — women 16pp less likely, employer restrictions hinder broader use.

sources.title: The Projected Impact of Generative AI on Future Productivity Growth
sources.excerpt: In about 40% of employment in exposed occupations, at least 50% of tasks will be replaceable. Average labor-cost savings ~25% from current tools, potentially 40% as systems improve.

sources.title: The Anthropic Economic Index: Economic Primitives
sources.excerpt: 49% of jobs now use AI for at least 25% of their tasks (up from 36% in early 2025); widespread adoption could boost US labor productivity by 1.0-1.8 percentage points annually.

sources.title: Uneven geographic and demographic patterns of AI adoption
sources.excerpt: Only ~25% of Information sector businesses using AI; ~2.5% in Accommodation/Food — adoption patterns driven more by workforce composition than income.

sources.title: AI, Productivity, and Labor Markets: A Review of the Empirical Evidence
sources.excerpt: 35.9% of US workers used generative AI by December 2025; adoption is accelerating but remains unevenly distributed across industries and skill levels.

sources.title: AI's Impact on Job Growth
sources.excerpt: Less than 10% of firms using AI regularly as of mid-2025 (BTOS data); ~20% adoption in professional, scientific, and technical industries.

sources.title: Is AI Already Replacing Jobs? A Large-Scale Survey
sources.excerpt: 37.4% of US workers used AI on the job in the past week. Adoption highest among college-educated (52%) and workers earning $100K+ (58%). Survey of 25,000 workers.

sources.title: Gallup Workplace AI Adoption Survey Q4 2025
sources.excerpt: 46% of US workers reported using AI tools at work in Q4 2025, up from 33% in Q1 2025. Adoption driven by white-collar professional and technical roles.

sources.title: Firm Data on AI
sources.excerpt: 69% of firms across US, UK, Germany, and Australia currently use some AI technology (US: 78%). LLM text generation most common (41%). Expected to rise to 75% in 3 years. Larger, more productive, higher-paying firms more likely to adopt.

sources.title: The State of AI: Agents, Innovation, and Transformation (Nov 2025)
sources.excerpt: 88% of organizations use AI in ≥1 function (up from 78%). Gen AI adoption at 71%. But only 7% fully scaled, and just 6% report EBIT impact ≥5%. 62% experimenting with AI agents.

sources.title: Why 96% of Companies Aren't Seeing AI ROI
sources.excerpt: Survey of 180 Fortune 100 executives and 12,000 knowledge workers. 96% of organizations not seeing dramatic improvements in efficiency, innovation, or work quality from AI. Costing Fortune 500 ~$98B/year in lost returns. Workers report feeling 33% more productive individually, but organizational metrics flat.

sources.title: AI-Generated 'Workslop' Is Destroying Productivity
sources.excerpt: Survey of 1,150 US workers: 40% received AI-generated 'workslop' in the past month; each instance cost ~2 hours to deal with. 18% of AI users admitted sending low-quality AI output. Estimated cost: $186/worker/month or ~$9M/year for a 10,000-person org.

sources.title: January 2026 US Labor Market Update: Jobs Mentioning AI Are Growing Amid Broader Hiring Weakness
sources.excerpt: The Indeed AI Tracker reached a high of 4.2% in December 2025...the number of postings mentioning AI measured 134% above February 2020 levels

sources.title: Fault Lines
sources.excerpt: The United States has seen 50% growth in AI-related postings over the past year, with AI now appearing in 2.5% of all job postings.

sources.title: State of IT jobs: AI sparks rapidly changing market for skills
sources.excerpt: 80% of respondents in the 2025 Indeed Workforce Insights Report report they save at least one hour per day using generative AI. Job postings that require AI literacy skills are growing at a rate of more than 70% year over year.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence: friend or foe for hiring in Europe today?
sources.excerpt: Two-thirds of the 3,500 euro-area firms surveyed reported that their employees use AI in their jobs (ECB SAFE survey, Q4 2025). Note: European firms; not directly comparable to US Census BTOS figures.

sources.title: AI Will Displace…The Fed's View of Neutral
sources.excerpt: AI capex – roughly $650bn this year and potentially ~$2tn over three years – materially alters the equilibrium.

sources.title: Business Trends and Outlook Survey: Biweekly National Data Tables (AI Question)
sources.excerpt: In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in any of its business functions? Yes: 17.5%, No: 73.1%, Do not know: 9.4% (Cycle 202604, ref period Jan 26–Feb 8, 2026). First biweekly reading (Cycle 202524, Nov 2025): Yes: 17.3%.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Firm
sources.excerpt: Even 18 months after firm-level adoption, only about half of engineers had begun using the tools. Individual take-up was not universal.

sources.title: AI-fueled layoffs are rising, but a great divide is emerging
sources.excerpt: more than 71% said they have adopted AI tools either 'somewhat' or 'extensively,' while just under 20% said they were considering it either for this year or later, and only 9% said they had no plans to adopt the technology.

sources.title: Research on AI and the labor market is still in the first inning
sources.publisher: Peterson Institute for International Economics (Jed Kolko)
sources.excerpt: Current data from the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey shows that fewer than one-fifth of firms are using AI in any capacity, and even fewer are using AI directly for producing goods and services.

sources.title: What do professional software developers need to know to succeed in an age of Artificial Intelligence?
sources.excerpt: Generative AI is showing early evidence of productivity gains for software developers

sources.title: Evidence on the Adoption of Artificial Intelligence: The Role of Skills Shortage
sources.excerpt: Skills shortage has a positive and significant effect on AI adoption breadth and application areas (German Mannheim Innovation Panel).

sources.title: Enterprise AI Adoption Survey
sources.excerpt: 72% of enterprise leaders use AI weekly; 62% of companies actively use AI (n=800).

sources.title: AI Adoption in US Firms
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York (Abel et al.)
sources.excerpt: Over 50% of information/finance firms use AI; few report layoffs from AI adoption.

sources.title: Information Nudges and AI Adoption
sources.excerpt: RCT shows information about AI productivity gains increases adoption among German firms.

sources.title: 2025 Work Trend Index
sources.excerpt: 75% of knowledge workers use AI at work; 78% bring own AI tools (n=31K, 31 countries).

sources.title: Is Distance from Innovation a Barrier to the Adoption of Artificial Intelligence?
sources.excerpt: A commuting zone which is an additional 200 km from the closest AI hotspot has 17% lower growth in AI jobs' share of vacancies. 20% of the effect is explained by state borders.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence, Productivity, and the Workforce: Evidence from Corporate Executives
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta / Duke University (Baslandze et al.)
sources.excerpt: 58.5% of ~750 surveyed firms invested in AI in 2025; 85.4% expect to invest in 2026. Many smaller firms only beginning to invest in 2026. Note: CFO Survey uses broader 'invested in AI' definition vs Census BTOS 'using AI in production', explaining higher rate.

sources.title: Pascual Restrepo on AI, Automation, and the Future of Work
sources.publisher: Yale Department of Economics (Restrepo, interviewed by Strathmann)
sources.excerpt: When you look at the data, adoption of AI by firms is still relatively low. Right now I would describe the labor market as more of a wait-and-see environment.

sources.title: State of AI in the Enterprise: The untapped edge
sources.excerpt: Nearly 3 in 4 (74%) companies plan to deploy agentic AI within two years. 34% are already starting to use AI to deeply transform their businesses—creating new products and services, reinventing core processes, or even fundamentally changing their business models.

sources.title: Firm Data on AI
sources.excerpt: Synthesizes firm-level survey data from the US, UK, Germany, and Australia measuring AI's realized and expected impacts on sales per employee and employment. Data collected Feb-Apr 2025 and Nov 2025-Jan 2026.

sources.title: McKinsey Global Survey on AI (State of AI, 2025)
sources.excerpt: 32% of companies expect AI to reduce workforce by 3%+ within next year. Median 17% of respondents report workforce declines within functions from AI use. 88% of organizations now use AI in at least one business function.

sources.title: Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) — AI Adoption Data, December 2025
sources.excerpt: AI adoption for production rose from 4.6% (early 2024) to 10% (Sep 2025). Broader measure (any business function): 17.3% (Nov 2025). 78.4% annualized growth rate. 80.9% of non-adopters cite inapplicability.

sources.title: AI use by individuals surges across the OECD as adoption by firms continues to expand
sources.excerpt: 36.8% of individuals across OECD used generative AI in 2025. 20.2% of firms used AI in 2025 (up from 8.7% in 2023). 41.1% of employed individuals used generative AI. 52.0% of large firms vs 17.4% small.

sources.title: Has Generative AI Adoption Impacted Labor Demand at Third District Firms?
sources.excerpt: About half of respondent firms in the Philadelphia Fed's Third District are using generative AI. Survey conducted late October 2025.

sources.title: The State of AI in the Enterprise — 2026 AI Report
sources.excerpt: 71% of organizations regularly use generative AI in at least one business function (up from 65% in early 2024). 92% plan to invest in generative AI over next three years. 66% report productivity gains.

sources.title: Mind the Gap: AI Adoption in Europe and the U.S.
sources.excerpt: Firm encouragement alone accounts for 80% of the overall average gap.

sources.title: AI Quarterly Pulse Survey Q1 2026
sources.excerpt: Today, more than half of organizations are actively deploying AI agents.

sources.title: The Enterprise AI Playbook: Lessons from 51 Successful Deployments
sources.publisher: Stanford Digital Economy Lab (Pereira, Graylin, Brynjolfsson)
sources.excerpt: Agentic implementations are currently a minority at 20% of cases.

sources.title: Economists Once Dismissed the A.I. Job Threat, but Not Anymore
sources.excerpt: Already, nearly one in five companies reports having used A.I. in the last two weeks, according to data from the Census Bureau, and in some industries the rate is twice as high.

sources.title: AI Adoption by Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
sources.publisher: OECD (Calvino, Bianchini, Lane, Montegu, Verger, Ancheva)
sources.excerpt: AI adoption in core business functions – related to the production of goods and services – ranges from 1.9% in Japan to 6.1% in the United States in 2024. Among SMEs using generative AI, only 29% report using it in their core activities.

sources.title: Mapping AI into Production: A Field Experiment on Firm Performance
sources.publisher: INSEAD / Harvard Business School (Kim, Kim, Koning)
sources.excerpt: Treated firms discover 2.7 additional AI use cases (a 44% increase), concentrated in product development and strategy. The binding constraint is not access to the technology but the ability to discover where they create value and how to reorganize the firm accordingly.
